subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should every ClickClack REST operation use one fixed 30-second deadline, and should callers be allowed to override that deadline through the exported client API?
rationale: ClickClack is self-hosted, its docs do not define a request-duration contract, and the proposed test override changes a public plugin barrel, so repository history cannot determine the intended compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Private fixed deadline
options.body: Keep 30 seconds as an owner-local constant, remove the exported override, use fake timers in tests, and require controlled real-HTTP proof before merge.

options.title: Intentional API option
options.body: Retain `requestTimeoutMs` only after explicitly approving and documenting it as a supported ClickClack plugin API with compatibility coverage.

options.title: Operation-specific deadlines
options.body: Use different internal deadlines when legitimate message reads, activity writes, or future uploads have materially different timing requirements.

recommendation.title: Private fixed deadline
recommendation.body: Keep 30 seconds as an owner-local constant, remove the exported override, use fake timers in tests, and require controlled real-HTTP proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged ClickClack work owns the principal REST callers and activity behavior affected by the new deadline.
